CEA-4c(a)(1).summary: Prohibits transactions that are, or are commonly known as, wash sales or accommodation trades, and fictitious sales.
CEA-4c(a)(1).title: Commodity Exchange Act, wash sales and fictitious trades

CEA-4c(a)(5).summary: Makes it unlawful to violate bids or offers, to show intentional or reckless disregard for the orderly execution of transactions during the closing period, or to spoof ("bidding or offering with the intent to cancel the bid or offer before execution").
CEA-4c(a)(5).title: Commodity Exchange Act, disruptive practices

CFTC-180.summary: Prohibits the use of any manipulative device, scheme or artifice to defraud, and the manipulation or attempted manipulation of the price of any swap, commodity or future.
CFTC-180.title: Prohibition on manipulative and deceptive devices and price manipulation

CFTC-38.251.summary: Requires a contract market to adopt rules and pre-trade risk controls that prevent, detect and mitigate market disruptions and system anomalies associated with electronic trading.
CFTC-38.251.title: Electronic trading risk principles for designated contract markets

CME-534.summary: Prohibits placing or accepting buy and sell orders in the same product for accounts with common beneficial ownership where the orders are expected to match each other.
CME-534.title: Wash trades prohibited

CME-575.summary: All orders must be entered for the purpose of executing bona fide transactions; prohibits orders entered to mislead, to overload or delay systems, or to disrupt orderly trading.
CME-575.title: Disruptive practices prohibited

FINRA-5210.citation: FINRA Rule 5210, Supplementary Material .02 (self-trades) and .03 (disruptive quoting and trading)
FINRA-5210.summary: Prohibits publishing quotations or transactions that are not bona fide. The supplementary material covers self-trades from related algorithms and the entry of orders on one side to move the market before trading on the other.
FINRA-5210.title: Publication of transactions and quotations

MAR-12.citation: Regulation (EU) No 596/2014, Articles 12 and 15, with Annex II of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/522
MAR-12.summary: Defines and prohibits market manipulation. The delegated regulation lists the practices that indicate it, among them layering and spoofing, quote stuffing, wash trades, momentum ignition and marking the close.
MAR-12.title: Market Abuse Regulation, market manipulation

MIFID2-RTS6.summary: Requires pre-trade controls (price collars, maximum order value and volume, maximum message limits), real-time monitoring, post-trade controls and a kill function for algorithmic trading, plus automated surveillance for market manipulation.
MIFID2-RTS6.title: Organisational requirements for algorithmic trading

MIFID2-RTS9.summary: Requires trading venues to calculate, for each member, the ratio of unexecuted orders to transactions both by number and by volume, and to set maximum ratios.
MIFID2-RTS9.title: Ratio of unexecuted orders to transactions

SEA-9(a).summary: Prohibits wash sales and matched orders entered to create a false or misleading appearance of active trading, and series of transactions that raise or depress a price to induce others to trade.
SEA-9(a).title: Securities Exchange Act, manipulation of security prices

SEC-10b-5.summary: The general anti-fraud rule: prohibits any device, scheme or act that operates as a fraud or deceit in connection with the purchase or sale of a security.
SEC-10b-5.title: Employment of manipulative and deceptive devices

SEC-15c3-5.summary: Requires a broker-dealer with market access to maintain risk management controls that prevent orders exceeding pre-set credit or capital thresholds and reject erroneous orders (by price or size), and to review their effectiveness regularly.
SEC-15c3-5.title: Market Access Rule

LIM-01.description: The net position in either instrument went beyond the exchange's position limit.
LIM-01.title: Position limit

LIM-02.description: The combined ETF and future position stayed outside the un-hedged allowance for longer than permitted. A warning is raised when most of the permitted time has been used.
LIM-02.title: Un-hedged exposure

LIM-03.description: Order messages were sent faster than the exchange's throttle allows: the participant reached the limit and the exchange disconnected it. A warning is raised as the rate approaches the limit.
LIM-03.title: Message rate

MKT-01.description: Large orders were repeatedly shown in the visible part of the book on one side while the participant traded on the other, then withdrawn unexecuted, by cancelling them or amending them down, without being replaced.
MKT-01.title: Spoofing and layering

MKT-02.description: Two participants traded with each other in both directions in matching size, and either did most of their business with each other or passed the same lots straight back at a matching price, so that nothing changed hands and no risk was taken.
MKT-02.title: Wash trading

MKT-03.description: Bursts of orders were entered and cancelled almost at once with nothing executed, a pattern that loads the exchange and obscures the book without any intent to trade.
MKT-03.title: Quote stuffing

MKT-04.description: In the final seconds of the session the participant paid through fair value in a way that moved the closing price in favour of the position it was holding.
MKT-04.title: Marking the close

MKT-05.description: The ratio of order messages to executions, counted as MiFID II RTS 9 counts them, was far above what a participant trading in good faith produces.
MKT-05.title: Order-to-trade ratio

MKT-06.description: An order was priced so far from the market that it is either an error or an attempt to print an unrepresentative price.
MKT-06.title: Off-market order

REC-01.description: A trade or hedge reported by the exchange is not the one obtained by replaying the order stream through the matching rules, the positions the stream adds up to are not those on the exchange's score board, or the stream is incomplete, out of order or unreadable.
REC-01.title: Trade reconciliation
